static_traits.name: Liu Jie
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive spouse and friends, but discussion of this belief is rare and feels difficult
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems in the past; not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic, able to self-Reflect and identify strengths; slightly tense at first but Positive attitude, high cooperation

basic_info.main_problem: I believe I am only good at being an Athlete, and this belief limits my exploring other aspects of life.
basic_info.core_demands: Seeking counseling because I realize this belief hinders my Personal growth and brings dissatisfaction; hoping through reality testing and other methods to develop a more accurate, constructive understanding of my abilities and potential beyond being an Athlete, boost confidence and satisfaction in trying new things, and find better balance between family and career.
growth_experiences: After succeeding in a racing career, gradually feeling trapped by the single identity of 'race car driver'; social expectations and personal insecurity trigger and reinforce the belief of 'only good at being an Athlete'. Since then, Self-doubt and negation repeatedly surface whenever considering new opportunities (like coaching, starting a business, or new hobbies); tried interests like cooking and painting but quickly gave up because of 'I cannot do it', long affecting performance in non-competitive areas and Family relationships, making daily life feel stagnant and dissatisfying.

core_beliefs: I can do nothing except being an Athlete
My worth comes only from athletic performance

special_situations.event: When considering career transition or Personal growth opportunities (like coaching young drivers, starting a business, or developing new hobbies)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do well quickly like in racing, it means I have no ability and should not try
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating or shrinking attempts in advance in one's mind, staying only at the idea stage and maintaining the existing 'race car driver' identity to avoid failure and being negated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I definitely cannot do these, I will fail

special_situations.event: When actually trying new hobbies (such as cooking, painting), meets beginner-stage setbacks
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do well right away, it proves I am not good at it and have no talent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Quickly gives up new activities to reduce frustration and shame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot do it, cannot learn it

special_situations.event: Feeling 'trapped' by a single identity after racing career success, triggered by social expectations and personal insecurity
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only by maintaining a top Athlete identity am I worthy of recognition; leaving this identity means having no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Binds self-worth to outside evaluation, tends to consider only racing-related paths (such as instruction) to lower risk
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Others only recognize me as an Athlete; I can only do this

special_situations.event: When spending time with family and trying to find life balance outside racing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not do well in family roles, it proves I am not competent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Retreating to familiar Work and identity domains, reducing investment in family to avoid competence Anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot be a good husband/Father

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen and recognized in multiple roles and domains beyond racing, gaining a more complete sense of self-worth and Freedom of choice
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure after leaving the 'top Athlete' identity, being negated and losing value and respect in relationships, leading to self-disintegration
defense_goal: Controlling uncertainty by maintaining a single and successful Athlete identity, reducing the risk of failure and being negated
Avoids new attempts and emotional exposure, to maintain self-esteem and a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent self in non-competitive domains, prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Others/society who judge me by achievements and performance, only recognizing me as an Athlete
object_relations.linking_affect: Anxiety, shame, sense of being restricted

object_relations.self_representation: A self who wants to invest more in family but feels limited and unable to balance
object_relations.object_representation: Family who are supportive but may be let down by me (wife and daughter)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others encourage them to explore identities and abilities beyond racing, or invite trying new activities
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing invitations as tests of ability: if not immediately excellent, will be negated (Projecting social expectations onto others in the present)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Ending the topic dismissively with reasons like 'not much interest/limited time/not suitable', in a steady tone but avoiding details and emotions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to express the vulnerable experience of 'only being an Athlete' more candidly with family or significant others
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worries exposing vulnerability will lead to being looked down on or losing respect, thus keeps distance from emotions
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using objective, generalized wording, not touching emotional vocabulary; restrained, measured tone, focusing on facts and arrangements rather than feelings.

manifestations: Feeling 'trapped' by a single identity after racing success, struggling to make new choices in the face of social expectations and self-insecurity
Whenever considering new opportunities, being intercepted by doubt and negation, experiencing restricted freedom of choice
outcomes: Avoiding and giving up new attempts

manifestations: Daily life feeling stagnant and dissatisfying
Performance in non-competitive domains is limited; hard to develop a new sense of worth
outcomes: Decreased drive, quickly giving up new activities
Single attachment of self-worth leading to emptiness

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Repeatedly uses social expectations as a reference, believes only by maintaining the 'race car driver' identity is one recognized
Internalizes external evaluation as the sole standard of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Quickly doubting oneself when discussing new attempts: 'I cannot do it'
Setting excessively high standards for non-competitive domains, evaluating success and failure in an all-or-nothing way

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Rarely proactively seeks support from spouse and friends regarding this belief
Turning outward energy into self-negation and giving up new activities

positive_force: Support network of spouse and friends present
Self-reports having the ability to motivate others and a fast learning speed
Already able to identify and willing to challenge negative thinking patterns (Positive attitude, willing to act)
Proposes feasible small-step actions (communicating with his wife, trying to mentor young drivers)
negative_force: Binding self-worth solely to the 'Athlete' identity
All-or-nothing thinking, overgeneralization, predicting the future and other cognitive biases reinforcing Self-denial
Dependence on external evaluation and Introjected social expectations
Quickly giving up new activities due to initial setbacks, forming avoidance and learned helplessness
Hard to open up to relatives and friends about core beliefs, reducing opportunities for calibration and support

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids or quickly abandons new attempts in non-competitive areas
antecedent: When considering career transition or Personal growth opportunities
When starting a new hobby (such as cooking, painting) and encountering beginner-stage setbacks
When facing social expectations or self-comparison
target_behavior.core_reason: Negative core belief 'I can do nothing except being an Athlete'; all-or-nothing thinking, overgeneralization and predicting failure; Fear of being negated and dependence on external evaluation
target_behavior.function: Avoids failure and shame; maintains a familiar and safe self-concept and identity
target_behavior.consequence: Performance and development in non-competitive domains hindered, interests hard to sustain, Personal growth stagnating with dissatisfaction

target_behavior.behavior: Insufficient investment in family roles, struggling to balance with the racing career
antecedent: Returning to family life after a busy competition schedule
When thinking about undertaking more family roles or arranging time with family
When feeling 'trapped' by a single identity
target_behavior.core_reason: Role-competence Anxiety and Self-denial triggered by a single self-identity (worrying about not doing well in husband/Father roles)
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible failure experiences in family roles, maintaining a sense of control and certainty over the 'Athlete' identity
target_behavior.consequence: Connection with wife and daughter affected, increased subjective distance and dissatisfaction
